answer: Sybil resistance here rests on slashed stake, not just locked stake. Registering a key needs a bond larger than one identity's expected reward, and payouts require a pulse signed by that key each window. When many keys answer one pulse from the same operator, the cluster collapses and every bond burns. A dawn snapshot before payouts stops identities being stacked afterwards, while a pigment tag per operator shows duplicate clusters without real names. A fake identity thus costs a bond plus total-loss risk, so a thousand clones means a thousand bonds at risk.
